message:
I am thinking...: Now I can see the bug. The `insn_name_maps[]` array only has 3 entries:
1. `{ TMS320C64X_INS_INVALID, NULL }` 
2. `{ TMS320C64X_INS_ADD, "add" }`
3. `{ TMS320C64X_INS_NOP, "nop" }`

But `TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING` is a much larger value (after all the instructions defined in the header, it's at line 328). The check `if (id >= TMS320C64X_INS_ENDING) return NULL;` will pass for any valid instruction ID, but then `insn_name_maps[id].name` will access out of bounds because the array only has 3 elements.

So any TMS320C64X instruction with id > 2 (i.e., anything beyond ADD and NOP) will trigger the global buffer overflow.

To trigger this, I need:
1. First byte selects TMS320C64X architecture (item 27 in the "next" version with 29 platforms)
2. Remaining bytes form a valid TMS320C64X instruction that decodes to an instruction with id > 2

For the "next" version, `platforms_len` = 29 (items 0-28, includes WASM).
Data[0] % 29 == 27 means Data[0] could be 27.

TMS320C64X uses big-endian mode. I need to provide bytes that will decode to a valid TMS320C64X instruction. Let me look at how TMS320C64X instructions are encoded.

Let me check what instruction encodings exist. TMS320C64X uses 32-bit fixed-length instructions (4 bytes).
